# Windows UCRT fresh Mainnet write comparison

The workflow tests asynchronous RPC dispatch and owned-process cleanup before downloading the checkpoint. Every replay and reopen records a separate cleanup receipt; an RPC exception, cancellation or forced process exit cannot qualify as a clean shutdown. Listener cleanup closes its owned peer transports before waiting for the server to finish. Failed measurements and cleanup receipts remain available for diagnosis.

One standard Windows Server 2022 AMD64 Actions job runs the fixed sequence reference, bounded32, bounded32, reference. It retains the existing timeout-fixed reference artifact from run 45926384208 and the timeout-fixed bounded32 candidate artifact from run 45929224054. Complete release-input checksums, source SHA/tree markers and the daemon's native PE32+ identity are checked before launch. The workflow builds only the standalone raw evidence exporter against the vendored LevelDB tree shared by both native packages. Product binaries are unchanged.

The exact public `en8-mainnet-tail-fixture-v1` is downloaded and restored once. The small diagnostic `en8-fresh-mainnet-tail-overlay-v1` release supplies the independently verified pre-anchor recipe and real block corpus. Its overlay manifest and archive, original cursor receipt, genuine anchor header and 4,096-block body stream all have exact embedded pins. Each case uses a separately reconstructed and hashed receiver and an empty configuration. A restored source stays closed for the entire sequence. Capacity checks reserve space for compressed parts, the base, one complete target and 8 GiB overhead. Data preparation and hashing are outside the scored intervals.

## Matching and measurements

The compiled Windows defaults select a 1,024 MiB database cache and automatic script-check parallelism. Startup enforces the observed 64 MiB block-index, 8 MiB coin database and 952 MiB in-memory UTXO allocations. The candidate must log the nominal 32-table policy on the admitted RAM class. The reference must omit that marker. The original Linux qualification uses 128 MiB and two script-check participants as explicit isolation settings. Its timings are not a comparator arm.

Each receiver verifies the same 44,942,101 tip, UTXO and stock historical proof scan to completion before enabling an ordinary loopback peer. Block/header proof and work floors are unchanged. The test requests full script verification with `-assumevalid=0`. The peer answers stock GETHEADERS and GETDATA with authenticated Mainnet records and no forced ingress pauses. Each arm checks all accepted header-batch endpoints, block requests and receipts, active tip, ConnectTip and undo counts, and the exact final UTXO. Stock RPC forced sync must log the ordered block/undo, index and positive changed-coins stages. An offline reopen verifies the same state with clean exits on both starts.

Native counters record CPU time, working set, process working-set peak, private committed usage, and process I/O operations and bytes at named boundaries. Process I/O can include cache, pipe and other I/O, so it is distinct from storage-device bytes. Sync stages and the combined UTXO scan use separate timings. Bracket ratios report both comparisons without repeats or best-case selection. The interval exercises genuine fresh writes and one explicit flush. It is too short to establish normal full-IBD compaction cadence or predict a whole-chain duration.

Each sample has a 16-minute owned replay deadline followed by bounded cleanup if required. Startup, history, delivery and shutdown have separate finite deadlines. The single job has a 100-minute maximum including downloads, small exporter build, preparation and evidence retention. Any incomplete configuration or sample is recorded and fails the workflow.

## Closed storage evidence

The raw flat-file check starts at the separately pinned original file-169 body and undo ends. It compares all 4,096 fresh bodies with the known requested bytes and all undo records with their canonical parents, transaction counts and independently established digest. `flat-file-positions.json` lists canonical display hashes and their new payload offsets and sizes. These positions are independent of the database's reported offsets.

The bounded exporter opens only the closed disposable receiver under the job's private scratch directory. It reads raw records and verifies LevelDB checksums. LevelDB may update its physical open or log metadata on this disposable copy. The exporter performs no logical writes. `index-export.bin` starts with eight ASCII bytes `SCIDX01\n` and a 32-bit little-endian record count of 8,243. Each record contains a one-byte presence flag, one-byte key length, two-byte little-endian value length, serialized raw key and stored raw value. Absent records have a zero value length. The file ends after the last record, and the complete export is bounded to 1 MiB.

Rows begin with the optional serialized obfuscation-key record, the required file-169 metadata and the required last-file row. The rest are raw b/y pairs in anchor, ascending canonical height, then sorted display-hash fork order. The 23 forks must be absent in both key spaces. The exact request SHA-256 is `63d2616c77a3acf7289130e77cbff4005189fe267d4fadd580ca193d8f10f6d6`, derived from the pinned anchor, tail and audited fork list. The evidence receipt binds the complete raw payload, flat-file positions, package provenance and replay result digests. These compact artifacts survive receiver cleanup. Independent stock typed decoding must confirm each index row's header, height, status, proof binding, and body/undo offsets before considering an adoption decision.
